land.text: the lands John of Islay held from Edward Balliol in 1336, 'the territories which the Islay lords had acquired in the days of Robert I'

predecessors.note: The title 'began with Somerled in the 12th century' (Lordship page) and the Kingdom of the Isles was ceded to Scotland in 1266; the Lordship's lands were held from the Scottish crown.

land.text: 'In 1493, the Parliament of King James IV of Scotland finally brought the independent Lordship of the Isles to an end'; the Crown annexed Islay and the other isles in 1540

capitals.name: Finlaggan (Islay)
capitals.note: 'Finlaggan on Islay was the seat of the Lords of the Isles under Somerled and Clan Donald.'

correction.text: Islay, Jura, Colonsay, Gigha, Mull, Morvern and Lewis, the lands John of Islay held after 1336 (Kintyre, Knapdale and Skye, also named in Balliol's grant, are left out)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe; Cliopatria has no Lordship of the Isles (its Kingdom of the Isles row ends in 1176, the Scotland row draws the Hebrides in 1294-1493). 'Edward awarded John the lands of Kintyre, Knapdale, Gigha, Colonsay, Mull, Skye, Lewis, and Morvern', but the page says Balliol's deposition made the grants void and 'John's pre-1336 possessions were confirmed by King David in 1343'; Kintyre and Knapdale reappear as a dowry in 1350 and Skye comes with Ross in 1438, so those three are added at those dates. Circles of radius 22-35 km stand for the islands (res-5 cells, about 250 km2); the Islay circle reaches the west coast of Kintyre and the seaboard circle the south of Skye, so those two are not clean edges.

correction.text: the Lordship after Garmoran: 'all of the Hebrides except Skye, and all of the western seaboard from Morvern to Loch Hourn'

keyframe_review.note: 'In 1346, John inherited the great Lordship of Garmoran through his marriage to Amie mac Ruari.' The Outer Hebrides are the Eilean Siar council area, the inner isles are circles, the seaboard a 35 km circle at Moidart. The page gives no area.

correction.text: the 1346 shape plus Knapdale and Kintyre

keyframe_review.note: 'In 1350, John was given Robert's daughter Margaret Stewart in marriage, and received Knapdale and Kintyre as dowry.'

The 1376 charters 'granted Lochaber to John and his Stewart wife together'. Lochaber is a 30 km circle at Fort William; the John MacDonald page does not mention it, so it stays drawn to 1475 in the absence of a loss date.

correction.text: the 1376 shape plus the earldom of Ross and Skye

keyframe_review.note: The Hebrides, 'including Skye and Ross', were held 'from 1438' (Lordship page); Alexander of Islay is 'Earl of Ross and Lord of the Isles' (John MacDonald page). Ross is a 50 km circle at 57.72 N 4.75 W; it takes in the Inverness margin because the page gives no boundary.

correction.text: the Hebrides, Lochaber and the seaboard, without Ross, Skye, Knapdale and Kintyre

keyframe_review.note: In 1476 John 'lost the earldom of Ross - with the Isle of Skye - as well as Knapdale and Kintyre' but 'retained control of the Hebrides'.

region.text: Islay, Jura, Colonsay, Gigha, Mull, Morvern and Lewis

ledger.note: 1336: John of Islay becomes 'lord of the isles (1336-1386)'. 'In 1336, Edward confirmed the territories which the Islay lords had acquired in the days of Robert I'; 'Edward awarded John the lands of Kintyre, Knapdale, Gigha, Colonsay, Mull, Skye, Lewis, and Morvern'; the deposition of Balliol voided these and 'John's pre-1336 possessions were confirmed by King David in 1343'. The Lordship page gives no founding year (it says the title began with Somerled in the 12th century; Somerled 'seized the Isles' in 1135 and gained Man in 1156).

region.text: the Outer Hebrides, the rest of the inner isles except Skye, and the seaboard from Morvern to Loch Hourn

ledger.note: 1346: Garmoran comes by marriage. 'In 1346, John inherited the great Lordship of Garmoran through his marriage to Amie mac Ruari'; 'This meant that John's dominions now included all of the Hebrides except Skye, and all of the western seaboard from Morvern to Loch Hourn.' Counterpart is the page's name for the inherited lordship (Raghnall Mac Ruaidhrí, her brother, held it).
1350: 'John was given Robert's daughter Margaret Stewart in marriage, and received Knapdale and Kintyre as dowry' (Robert, later Robert II).
1376: the charters 'granted Lochaber to John and his Stewart wife together' (Robert II section). The page gives the year and the land, not the extent; the John MacDonald page never mentions Lochaber.

region.text: the earldom of Ross and Skye

ledger.note: 1438: Ross and Skye are held with the Hebrides. 'The Hebrides, including Skye and Ross, were held from 1438' (Lordship page); the John MacDonald page names Alexander as 'Earl of Ross and Lord of the Isles' without a year (the usual 1437 is not on either page), and John succeeded in 1449 'while a still a minor'.
mid-1470s: 'John was summoned before parliament to answer for his treasons, and when he failed to appear was declared forfeit.' The page says only 'mid-1470s', so 1475 is a bridge (confidence 1).
summer 1476: the settlement. 'He lost the earldom of Ross' at the peace of 1476 (the page places the loss in 1476, not 1475).

region.text: the earldom of Ross with Skye, Knapdale and Kintyre

ledger.note: 1476: 'He lost the earldom of Ross - with the Isle of Skye - as well as Knapdale and Kintyre' but 'retained control of the Hebrides'. The Scotland dossier has no matching 1476 gain.

region.text: the Hebrides and the remaining mainland holdings

ledger.note: 1493: 'In 1493, the Parliament of King James IV of Scotland finally brought the independent Lordship of the Isles to an end.' The Lordship page: 'Upon the discovery of his alliance with Edward IV in 1493,' James IV took John II's lands, estates and titles (the 1462 treaty with Edward IV is the alliance; in 1540 James V annexed 'Islay and the other Isles to the Crown').

wars.name: Forfeiture of Ross and the Lordship
wars.outcome: John summoned before parliament in the mid-1470s, declared forfeit, and in 1476 lost the earldom of Ross with Skye, Knapdale and Kintyre but kept the Hebrides; the Lordship itself was forfeit in 1493.
wars.note: The Treaty of Westminster-Ardtornish (February 1462: 'John's representatives concluded an agreement' envisaging the division of Scotland, with John paying homage to Edward IV for help gaining the lands north of the Forth) is the alliance behind the 1493 forfeiture; the Lordship page says only that John II signed a treaty with Edward IV in 1462.

certainty.note: The pages give lands by name, not boundaries; the shapes are circles round the named islands and glens.

sources.title: John of Islay, Lord of the Isles

notes: The Scotland dossier (kingdom-of-scotland) draws the Hebrides as a vassal tint under the counterpart string 'Lordship of the Isles' from 1294 to 1493; this page-dated Lordship begins only in 1336, and for the years 1294-1335 the page names no lord. When the compiler pairs the two, the string should become this slug; the Scotland vassal region should then be cut to the lands held (or the lords' own shape drawn alone and the vassal tint dropped). Not mapped: Somerled's kingdom (1135-1164; the Kingdom of the Isles dossier covers Mann and the Hebrides to 1266), the Battle of Harlaw (1411: Donald 'won' it; the page names no opponent), Domhnall Dubh (claimant, 1545). Alexander and Donald of Harlaw sit between John of Islay (d. 1386) and John MacDonald (lord 1449-1493) on pages not opened. The page budget was three pages.
